scope: Static reconstruction of auxiliary dynamic-array loading invoked by loader mode 5

activation.version_gate: Return immediately with ierr=0 when the active step version DAT_140b490f4 < 11000. This is not the database-header version DAT_140b490fc.
activation.effective_step_version: In the normal mode2/mode3 then mode5 sequence, 0x1403b6679 sets DAT_140b490f4 from selected row[8] for unified databases, or from the database-header version for legacy-signature databases.
activation.runtime_state_prerequisite: Mode5 checks DAT_140b490f4 before resolving its requested stored-step index. The original therefore depends on the previously established active-step state. A stateless C++ load_auxiliary(index) uses the selected step's effective version to reproduce the normal load-step-then-mode5 sequence; arbitrary original call histories are not modeled.
activation.zero_record_behavior: Return with ierr=0 without reading auxiliary data.
activation.positive_selector: Use supplied one-based stored-step index through step-table loader.
activation.nonpositive_selector: Search path compares step number with DAT_140707758; its initialization is not established by this dossier.

group_fields_zero_based.meaning: overwritten in memory with maximum positive decoded element count across entries; on-disk semantics not established
not used by inspected read/allocation routines; retain raw

metadata.payload_load_condition: group[0] > 0, independently of directory read condition
metadata.error_handling: Metadata/directory helper maps low-level nonzero I/O error to 1 after attempting word swapping. Top-level mode5 does not check this status before proceeding to allocation and payload readers.

entry_fields_zero_based.meaning: overwritten in memory with allocation index when entry[0] > 0; not a physical record or file byte offset
stored payload element count, including compression trailer
not used by inspected read/allocation routines; retain raw

directory.byte_order: all directory words swapped using normal int32 database conversion when the file/native mode requires it

allocation.real: entry[0] float64 elements, allocated as 2 * entry[0] int32 words when positive
allocation.temporary_integer: maximum expected integer count + 2 int32 elements
allocation.temporary_real: 2 * maximum expected real count + 4 int32 words

payload.compression: Unconditionally use the same backward run-link unpacking routines as regular arrays, including their trailing decoded-length and last-run-pointer elements.
low_level_order: Read the stored payload at entry[3].
Perform normal integer-word or float64 byte swapping for the database conversion mode.
Unpack even if the preceding read reported an error.
Map a nonzero I/O status to 1.
wrapper_order: Set ierr=0 on entry to the integer or real array wrapper.
Process all count entries in directory order; no positive-stored-count guard appears in the wrapper.
Call payload helper to obtain decoded element count.
Call the integer/real copy helper with the decoded count before checking status or expected count.
If ierr is nonzero or decoded count differs from entry[0], print diagnostic fields but continue to next entry.
payload.count_mismatch_status: No new error code is assigned for count mismatch alone.
payload.status_overwrite: The real wrapper resets ierr=0 and may mask earlier integer errors; subsequent low-level reads may replace earlier statuses. Exact malformed-input parity has not been run.

limitations: Schema describes fields consumed by these compiled readers. Retaining unused metadata/entry words is necessary because their meanings remain unknown.
No supplied fixture exercises auxiliary loading, so the schema is supported by static code only.
Ghidra output is recovered pseudocode, not original Fortran; overlapping globals and recovered signatures retain provider limitations.
Original unchecked reads, count-dependent allocation, and copying before error checking do not establish safe malformed-input semantics.
The initialization of DAT_140707758 for nonpositive step selectors remains unresolved.
No target executable was run by this auxiliary investigation.
